title: 📰 AI news · November 3

items.title: A virus asks an AI to price your stolen data
items.text: The VOLTA virus for Windows collects passwords, cookies, wallet phrases and cloud keys, then sends everything to Claude, Gemini or Kimi, which write a dossier on the victim. Your API keys and sessions sit where any program on your computer can see them. Check today where your bot's and project's keys are stored: in the browser, in notes or in files on disk. The free guide "Protecting your computer, code and access" is in the bot: send the word "protect".

items.title: Langflow has a hole: access without an account
items.text: Langflow, a builder for AI agents, has two critical flaws that let an outsider with no account run their own code on the server. Versions 1.0.0 to 1.12.8 are affected, and 1.13.0 has the fix. If you build agents or bots on Langflow, you keep AI-service keys and customer data there. Check your version and update today.

items.title: AI agents break into organizations on their own
items.text: CrowdStrike described a Chinese hacking campaign: the ARTEX tool, with several AI agents, was aimed at 200 organizations in 14 countries. The agents found weak spots and collected passwords themselves, and one break-in took 12 minutes. If your bot or site is open to the internet, a program can now find its weak spot in minutes. Check which accesses and passwords in your project have no protection.

items.title: Google shut down a botnet of 1.3 million TV boxes
items.text: Google seized the botnet's servers and banned the maker Videostrong from building certified Android devices. By Google's account, the company built a backdoor into the boxes itself and sold access to criminals.

items.title: Money is disappearing from BTCPay wallets
items.text: Attackers log in as administrators on BTCPay Server copies older than version 2.4.2 and drain hot wallets. If you accept crypto on your own server, update to version 2.4.7.

items.title: Anthropic: AI may soon improve itself
items.text: In its IPO filing, Anthropic wrote that it may soon reach the threshold of "dramatically accelerated progress due to AI". It does not place any current model beyond that threshold.

items.title: Goldman Sachs takes Claude Code away from bankers
items.text: The bank left AI coding tools to engineers only. Traders and bankers had used them for several months. The bank says the experimentation phase is over.

items.title: 50 AI agents in Minecraft built a bureaucracy
items.text: GPT-6.1 agents set up rations, fishing shifts and written shift handoffs in three hours. In games against Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 won 6:3 and 6:1.

items.title: Marvell buys Lumentum for 115 billion
items.text: The deal is all in shares and one of the biggest in tech history. Marvell wants to lead in connectivity for AI.

items.title: Spotify may charge up to $5 for AI remixes
items.text: That is what the Financial Times reports. Launch is named for the first quarter of 2027, and neither timing nor price is final.

takeaway: Three stories today point the same way: keys, access and open services are now found and taken by programs with AI, not by people. Recommendation: check where your bot's and project's keys are stored, and update every service you set up yourself.
